result.title: SCALE: Towards whole-slide counterfactual explanations in pathology
result.summary: Cancer diagnosis relies on histopathological evaluation, where tumor morphology guides disease classification and informs treatment decisions. Deep learning (DL) models excel at predicting diagnostic properties from histopathology images. Unlike typical medical images featuring small critical areas, histopathological images are textural, with relevant texture spanning the entire image; this makes it challenging to explain DL predictions by locating relevant image regions. Counterfactual explanations offer a promising alternative by asking "what changes in the image could have altered the model prediction." To achieve this, we propose SCALE, a framework for generating such counterfactual explanations for histopathological DL models. Across nine counterfactual directions spanning multiple cancer types, SCALE generates whole-slide counterfactual explanations that consistently shift predictions toward the intended target while maintaining biological feasibility. Blinded assessment by six board-certified pathologists showed higher morphological plausibility for SCALE (with a win rate of 91.7% over baselines) and promising counterfactual effectiveness (with a target consistency of 96.7%).

AI.brief_summary: SCALE 提出面向病理全切片的反事实解释框架，在九类癌症的九种反事实方向上生成能稳定把模型预测推向目标类别且保持生物学可行性的全切片图像，并由六位病理学家盲评。
AI.relevance_reason: 反事实图像生成可用于核查哪些视觉证据真正因果地影响模型判断，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与「答案是否使用视觉内容」的因果评价提供思路；但其属于病理分类的可解释性工作，不涉及多模态推理或 latent 状态生成，联系较远。
